source.title: On chromatic numbers of space-times: open problems

accepted.question_text: Determine the chromatic number χτ(R1,1) of the 2-dimensional Minkowski space-time R1,1, where χτ(R1,1) is the smallest number of colors in a coloring of R1,1 such that no two points A and B with temporal distance τ(A, B) = 1 receive the same color. In particular, is χτ(R1,1) finite?
accepted.context_brief: Temporal chromatic number of the Minkowski plane

evidence.quote: • χτ (R1,n), the smallest number of colors in a coloring of R1,n in which no two points A and B with τ (A, B) = 1 have the same color;
First open problem. What is the value of χτ (R1,1)? Is it finite?

accepted.question_text: For Minkowski space-time R1,n, interpret temporal distance 1 as one generation of proper time. What is the minimum number of colors or states needed so that any two events separated by proper time 1 must have different colors, i.e. what is χτ(R1,n) under this generational interpretation?

evidence.quote: A possible meaning of χτ (R1,n) is, e.g., that if we assume that we measure time in number of generations, then the events A and B corresponding to two immediately following generations should always be of different color.
In the relativistic case, as we have seen, two oscillating tastes are not enough, so how many do we need?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a system-changing process takes proper time 1 in Minkowski space-time. What is the smallest number of states needed so that whenever two objects coincide at the same space-time point they are always in the same state, under the requirement induced by a unit proper-time transition?

evidence.quote: An alternative, more physical meaning: let us assume that some system-changing process takes a proper time τ0 – hence, in the appropriate measuring units, the proper time 1.
What is the smallest number of states for which the two objects at the same point in space-time are always in the same state?

accepted.question_text: For a real parameter α ≥ 1, replace the usual Minkowski temporal and spatial distances by the Busemann metrics τα(A, B) = ((a0 − b0)^α − (a1 − b1)^α − ... − (an − bn)^α)^(1/α) when the expression is nonnegative, and ρα(A, B) = ((a1 − b1)^α + ... + (an − bn)^α − (a0 − b0)^α)^(1/α) when the expression is nonpositive. Determine the corresponding chromatic-number behavior for these generalized space-time metrics.

evidence.quote: Case of Busemann space-time metrics. What if instead of the Minkowski definitions of τ (A, B) and ρ(A, B), we take a real number α ≥ 1 and consider more general Busemann metrics

accepted.question_text: Let Rm,n be a pseudo-Euclidean space with quadratic form D(A, B) = (a1 − b1)^2 + ... + (am − bm)^2 − (am+1 − bm+1)^2 − ... − (am+n − bm+n)^2, temporal distance τ(A, B) = √D(A, B) when D(A, B) ≥ 0, and spatial distance ρ(A, B) = √(−D(A, B)) when D(A, B) ≤ 0. What are the corresponding chromatic numbers χτ(Rm,n) and χρ(Rm,n), and how do they relate to the Euclidean bounds χ(Rm) ≤ χτ(Rm,n) and χ(Rn) ≤ χρ(Rm,n)?

evidence.quote: Case of general pseudo-Euclidean spaces. What if we consider a general pseudo-Euclidean space Rm,n
• the temporal distance τ (A, B) = √D(A, B) which is defined when D(A.B) ≥ 0, and • the spatial distance ρ(A, B) = √−D(A, B), which is defined when D(A, B) ≤ 0.
Here also natural embeddings lead to χ(Rm) ≤ χτ (Rm,n) and χ(Rn) ≤ χρ(Rm,n).
